faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Quick answers to the most common questions.

items.question: How long does it take to get a driver's license?
items.answer: It depends on how quickly you complete the theory and driving lessons, but most people get their driver's license within 3–6 months.

items.question: Do you offer both manual and automatic transmission?
items.answer: Yes, we provide lessons in both manual and automatic transmission cars.

items.question: Can I get a driver's license if I am under 18?
items.answer: Yes, you can start theory and driving lessons from the age of 16 years and 9 months, but the practical test can only be taken at 17. When driving at 17, there are rules about having a supervising adult in the car.

items.question: How do the tests work?
items.answer: You must pass both a theoretical test and a practical driving test. We help you prepare for both.

items.question: Can I pay in installments?
items.answer: Yes, we offer flexible payment plans so you can pay for the driver's license in several installments without extra fees.

items.question: What happens if I don't pass the first time?
items.answer: No panic! You can sign up for a retest. We offer additional lessons to make sure you are ready next time. However, there will be a new fee to the Danish Road Traffic Authority, and if it is the driving test, there will also be a new payment for the car and the instructor's time.

items.question: Can I take a break during the course?
items.answer: Yes, you can. You are welcome to take a break from your lessons if needed and continue later. Contact us, and we will help you plan the rest of your course.

In addition, the VW Taigo is equipped with most of the safety features found in modern cars, helping to improve road safety. It is important that you learn how to deal with modern driver assistance systems, as future cars will increasingly be equipped with these technologies.

licenseCodes.title: What do the codes on your licence mean?
licenseCodes.description: Your Danish driving licence may contain codes describing rights, conditions, or restrictions. Click on a code to understand what it means for you.
licenseCodes.link78to148: Want the right to drive manual? See code 148

codes.label: Automatic only
codes.description: Issued when you have passed your driving test in an automatic car. The licence restricts you to vehicles with automatic transmission only.
codes.note: This is the standard code for all our students - you drive a VW Golf GTE.

codes.label: Right to drive manual
codes.description: Grants you the right to drive a manual car even though you originally passed in an automatic. Requires 7 hours of supplementary lessons with an approved driving instructor.
codes.note: If you want full freedom - both automatic and manual - you can add code 148 afterwards.

codes.label: Accompanied driving (age 17)
codes.description: Added for 17-year-olds who have passed their driving test. The code indicates a requirement for an accompanying driver until the young person turns 18.
codes.note: Only applies to students who start their licence at age 17.

codes.label: Administrative restriction
codes.description: An administrative code that may appear in special cases. The content depends on the specific case and is determined by the police or the Danish Road Directorate.
codes.note: This code is rare and will always be explained upon issue.

theoryPractice.title: We help you all the way to the theory test
theoryPractice.text1: You don't need to sit alone with the theory book. We go through everything important with you - and give you access to practice tests you can take whenever it suits you.
theoryPractice.text2: The practice tests are structured exactly like the real exam - same format, same difficulty, same types of questions.

features.title: Theory from the first lesson
features.text: We go through the theory in a structured way from the start - so you understand the rules, not just memorise them.

features.title: Access to practice tests
features.text: As our student you get access to practice tests you can take from home - as many times as you like, at your own pace.

features.title: At least 3 mock tests
features.text: We recommend a minimum of 3 run-throughs of the official mock test - spread over several days, not the night before.

theoryMistakes.title: The most common mistakes in the theory test
theoryMistakes.description: Most mistakes are not about lack of knowledge - but about attention, pace, and understanding of combined situations.

mistakes.title: Misreading situation images
mistakes.description: You see the image but miss the cyclist at the edge, the child behind the parked car, or the sign partially hidden by branches. Scan the whole image - not just the centre.

mistakes.title: Answering too quickly under time pressure
mistakes.description: You know the answer - but click the wrong one. The theory test gives plenty of time per question. Always read all the answer options, even if the first one seems obvious.

mistakes.title: Right of way at intersections
mistakes.description: Many know the rules in isolation but fail when they are combined in a specific situation. Shark teeth, dashed lines, and positioning in roundabouts are often tested together.

mistakes.title: Misinterpreting road signs
mistakes.description: Signs that look alike visually can have very different meanings. Supplementary signs below the main sign are often overlooked and completely change the message.

mistakes.title: Positioning and turning
mistakes.description: Questions about correct positioning before a turn, lane changes, and especially on multi-lane roads are classic traps - the rules are precise and require understanding.

mistakes.title: Alcohol and blood alcohol limits
mistakes.description: Many do not remember the exact limits for new and experienced drivers, or when a driving ban takes effect. This is concrete knowledge that is tested directly.

theoryTransition.checkLabel: Check before you book the test
checklist: You have understood right of way and positioning at intersections

reminder.text: You must have passed the theory test before you can book your final driving test. Valid for 18 months after passing.

theoryTransition.title: Passed the theory?

examChecklist.title: 8 things the examiner looks for
examChecklist.description: The examiner uses a fixed checklist throughout the entire driving test. Know the points before you get behind the wheel - so you know exactly what is being assessed.

items.title: Mirror use and shoulder check
items.text: Active use of all mirrors and turned shoulder when changing lanes and turning.

items.title: Road positioning
items.text: Correct positioning before turns, in roundabouts, and on multi-lane roads.

items.title: Speed adjustment
items.text: Keep the limit - and reduce speed in good time at junctions and uncertain situations.

items.title: Reaction to the unexpected
items.text: Do you spot and react correctly to cyclists, pedestrians, and cars that brake suddenly?

items.title: Signalling in time
items.text: Signals given well in advance - not at the same time as turning. Clear and timely signalling.

items.title: Right of way and junction behaviour
items.text: Mistakes at junctions are the most common cause of failure. The examiner watches every junction closely.

items.title: Turns and reversing manoeuvres
items.text: Calm and controlled execution counts more than speed. Typically a three-point turn.

items.title: Interaction with other road users
items.text: Considerate and clear behaviour towards cyclists, pedestrians, and other drivers.

examFail.title: Not passed?
examFail.description: It happens to many - and it is not the end of the world. Nearly 40% fail their driving test the first time. The most important thing is to understand exactly what went wrong and correct it in a targeted way.

steps.title: Understand what went wrong
steps.text: The examiner gives verbal feedback immediately after the test. Listen carefully - those are exactly the points we work on next.

steps.title: Focused review with your instructor
steps.text: We go through the mistakes specifically and make a plan for the next lessons. No general driving - only what was missing.

steps.title: Book a new test and drive it calmly
steps.text: You can book a new test within a few weeks. Most students pass on the second attempt - with the right preparation.

blogPage.title: Tips and news about driving
blogPage.description: Get insight into the theory test, driving test, and traffic rules.

hero.title: Looking for the "yellow car driving school"?
hero.subtitle: That is us - Lønbæks Køreskole in Vejle.

gulBil.intro: Many know us as the driving school with the yellow car - and that is not so strange. Our car is yellow, we are based in Vejle, and we have helped thousands of students get their licence since 1985. The official name is Lønbæks Køreskole, but no matter what you search for, you end up in the same place.
gulBil.whyTitle: Why do people search for "gul bil"?
gulBil.whyText1: Some remember us from the street. Others heard about us from a friend who mentioned the driving school with the yellow car in Vejle. It is one of those nicknames that just sticks.
gulBil.whyText2: We did not choose the name ourselves - but we are fine with it. And if you landed here, you found what you were looking for.
gulBil.aboutText: At Lønbæks Køreskole you get a personal driving education focused on both learning and wellbeing. Lessons are conducted at a calm pace so you feel well prepared for both the theory and practical test. With many years of experience in Vejle, we have helped thousands of students safely through their licence journey.

instructors.name: Anna Marie Lønbæk
instructors.bio: Anna Marie has been a driving instructor in Vejle since 1996 and has trained thousands of students. Her philosophy is simple: teaching should take place in a relaxed atmosphere to create the best conditions for learning.

instructors.name: Michael Lønbæk
instructors.bio: Michael has been a driving instructor since 1985 and is known for his calm and structured approach. He has extensive experience on driving technique courses and works with driving style evaluation for experienced drivers.

cars.name: VW Golf GTE
cars.text: The Golf GTE is an excellent school car with automatic transmission and all modern safety equipment. Students can focus on driving itself rather than technique - and will be ready for the new driving education requirements taking effect 1 July 2026.

cars.name: Volkswagen Taigo
cars.text: The Taigo is a stylish and technologically updated teaching car. Its compact size makes it ideal for city driving and longer trips, while modern assistance systems and dual controls ensure a safe and comfortable learning experience.

gulBil.strategyTitle: Four steps that make the difference

strategySteps.title: Individual assessment
strategySteps.text: We adapt lessons to your learning style and needs so you develop at your own pace.

strategySteps.title: Mock test
strategySteps.text: We drive almost the same test route under realistic conditions, so you know exactly what to expect.

strategySteps.title: Examiner training
strategySteps.text: We teach you exactly what the examiner looks for and how to score points during the test.

strategySteps.title: Stress management
strategySteps.text: Mental preparation and techniques to stay calm so nerves do not take over on the day.

gulBil.ctaTitle: Book a free meeting at the school
gulBil.ctaText: About 30 minutes. We go through your situation and make a plan. You pay nothing and commit to nothing.

handelsbetingelser.heading: Terms & Conditions
handelsbetingelser.intro: These terms apply to all services provided by Lønbæks Køreskole. By enrolling, you accept these terms in full.

general.title: 1. General
general.p1: These terms and conditions are governed by Danish law and apply to all purchases and services at Lønbæks Køreskole.

services.title: 2. Services
services.p1: Lønbæks Køreskole offers driving instruction for category B (car) licences, including theory lessons, practical driving, manoeuvring course, skid-pan training and preparation for theory and driving tests.

language.title: 3. Language of instruction
language.p1: Instruction is offered in Danish or English by arrangement. We reserve the right to terminate a course if communication is not working satisfactorily during lessons.

enrollment.title: 4. Enrolment
enrollment.p1: You can enrol by filling in the contact form on our website or by contacting us directly. We will get back to you to arrange the next steps.
enrollment.p2: All practical and financial details are agreed at a personal meeting at the driving school. You must be at least 18 years old to enter into the agreement. If you are under 18, prior consent from a parent or guardian is required.

payment.title: 5. Pricing & payment
payment.p1: Prices are provided upon personal enquiry at the driving school. Payment is made in cash or by bank transfer to the account number we provide at your visit. We do not accept payment via the website.

practical.title: 6. Practical matters
practical.p1: All other matters relating to your course — including cancellations, absences, breaks and consequences of non-attendance — are discussed and agreed at the start of your course at the driving school.

withdrawal.title: 7. Right of withdrawal
withdrawal.p1: As a consumer, you have a 14-day right of withdrawal from the date of the agreement, pursuant to the Danish Consumer Contracts Act. To exercise this right, you must notify us in writing before the deadline at hello@lønbæks.dk.
withdrawal.p2: If instruction has begun with your consent, you will be charged for services already delivered.

reviews.title: 8. Reviews
reviews.p1: After completing your course, we may ask you to leave a voluntary review of your experience. It is entirely up to you whether you wish to participate.

complaints.title: 9. Complaints & dispute resolution
